translations.source_sense_description: etwas, das sich höher befindet, von oben nach unten bewegen

glosses: To remove something from a wall or similar vertical surface to which it is fixed.

examples.text: He took down the picture and replaced it with the framed photograph.

glosses: To remove something from a hanging position.

examples.text: We need to take down the curtains to be cleaned.

glosses: To remove something from a website.

examples.text: We must take this fake news item down today.

glosses: To write down as a note, especially to record something spoken.

examples.text: If you have a pen, you can take down my phone number.
But if you ask me to bus my children / I hope the cops take down your name

glosses: To remove a temporary structure such as scaffolding.

examples.text: When everything else is packed, we can take down the tent.

glosses: To lower an item of clothing without removing it.

examples.text: The doctor asked me to take down my trousers.

glosses: To arrest someone or to place them in detention.

examples.text: We've got enough evidence now to take McFee down.
You have been found guilty. Take the prisoner down.
I took down the medicine and soon felt better.
Marcus Seltz, who can take down a bucket of crab legs like a freaking combine.

glosses: To defeat; to destroy or kill (a person).

examples.text: It took me eight years to get enough on the asshole to try and take him down.
They'd had occasion to see Peyton Armistead in all his righteous fury and she knew they wouldn't hesitate to take him down if she gave the word.
So Marinus, me and a few other unthanked individuals - Atemporals for the most part, with some mortal collaborators — make it our business to ...take them down.

glosses: To force one’s opponent off their feet in order to transition from striking to grappling in jujitsu, mixed martial arts, etc.
To collapse or become incapacitated from illness or fatigue.

examples.text: "[…]I mind the year after we came, my father took down with the ague, and things looked dark enough for a while; but, when old Billy Slater, on the Clear Fork killed a fat cow, he loaded a lot of the choicest on to a horse and brought it to us;[…]"
My brothers and sisters come working the fruit trees, / And they rode the truck till they took down and died.
to take the volume down a bit

translations.source_sense_description: etwas, das sich höher befindet, von oben nach unten bewegen

examples.text: Je baissai la vitre et roulai en écoutant les sons étouffés d’une fin de soirée d'été.
La fillette baissa d’abord la tête puis la releva craintivement et nous regarda.
Aussitôt l’intrus recula, baissa les yeux et, relevant les pans de sa pèlerine, affecta de se chauffer.

A l’époque du procès, cette femme pouvait avoir cinquante ans ; […]; sa voix était mielleuse, elle baissait la vue comme une vierge; en un mot, c’était une pateline dont l’aspect édifiant aurait suffi pour faire sortir un saint du purgatoire.
Baisser la voix. — Baisser un instrument de musique.

glosses: Diminuer la valeur vénale d’une chose.

examples.text: Baisser le prix d’une marchandise,

glosses: Diminuer de hauteur, rendre plus bas.

examples.text: Baisser une muraille, un toit, une maison.

— Au cours de l'année 1915, le blé, après avoir été pendant les premiers mois à 11 fr. 50 et 12 fr. 50 le moud d'environ 21 kilos, baissait graduellement jusqu'à 8 fr. 10 et même 7 fr. 30 en juillet et en août.
Nous nous embarquâmes, ma cousine et moi avec la fille de chambre, dans un petit bateau pour baisser la Loire.
Le baromètre a baissé terriblement pendant la nuit et la matinée. Je m’attends à du gros temps.
La rivière a baissé d’un pied.
La mer hausse et baisse deux fois le jour, par l’action du flux et du reflux.
Le jour baisse, le jour diminue, la nuit commence à venir.
Ce vieillard baisse, il s’affaiblit tous les jours.
Ce malade baisse, son état empire.
Sa vue commence à baisser, sa vue commence à n’être plus aussi bonne.
Son génie, son talent, son esprit baisse, il diminue, il s’affaiblit.
Ce vin baisse, il perd de sa force, de son bouquet.
Cette place de commerce baisse, elle perd de son commerce, de son crédit.
Cette marchandise baisse ; les actions, les rentes baissent ; les fonds publics baissent, le change baisse ; ils tombent, ils diminuent de prix, de valeur.
Les actions de cet homme baissent, Sa puissance, son crédit, sa réputation diminuent.
Son crédit, sa faveur baisse.

glosses: S’abaisser, se courber, se faire petit.

examples.text: Je me baissai pour ramasser le portefeuille et les cartes de visite qui s’étaient envolées dans le ruisseau.
Il faut se baisser, se baisser bien bas pour entrer dans cette grotte.
Baissez-vous davantage.
C’est un homme qui ne se hausse ni ne se baisse, il ne s’émeut de rien, il est toujours égal.
Baisser de rideau général jeudi pour les commerçants bressauds

examples.text: Quiero bajar WhatsApp; pero no sé cómo.

glosses: Disminuir el precio o costo de algo.

glosses: comparative form of low: more low
Bottom; more towards the bottom than the middle of an object.
Situated on lower ground, nearer a coast, or more southerly.

examples.text: Lower Manhattan
Lower Burgundy

tags: of strata or geological time periods

glosses: comparative form of low: more low
To let descend by its own weight, as something suspended; to let down

examples.text: lower a bucket into a well
to lower a sail of a boat

1833 (first publication), Alfred Tennyson, A Dream of Fair Women
Lower'd softly with a threefold cord of love
Down to a silent grave.

At level crossings where there are to be half-barriers, train-operated through track-circuiting, the barriers will be timed to lower fully about five seconds before the fastest train can reach the crossing.
to lower a flag
lower a fence or wall
lower a chimney or turret
lower the aim of a gun
to lower one's ambition, aspirations, or hopes

glosses: To reduce the degree, intensity, strength, etc., of

examples.text: lower the temperature
lower one's vitality
lower distilled liquors
Please lower your voices. This is a library.
lower one's pride

glosses: To humble oneself; to do something one considers to be beneath one's dignity.

examples.text: I could never lower myself enough to buy second-hand clothes.

glosses: To reduce (something) in value, amount, etc.

examples.text: lower the price of goods
lower the interest rate

glosses: To fall; to sink; to grow less; to diminish; to decrease

examples.text: The river lowered as rapidly as it rose.

glosses: To decrease in value, amount, etc.
To reduce operations to single machine instructions, as part of compilation of a program.

examples.text: Now is the winter of our diſcontent, / Made glorious ſummer by this ſonne of Yorke: / And all the cloudes that lowrd vpon our houſe, / In the deepe boſome of the Ocean buried.
[...] Juno took her place: / But ſullen Diſcontent ſat lowring on her Face.
And still when loudliest howls the storm, / And darkliest lowers his native sky, / The king's fierce soul is in that form, / The warrior's spirit threatens nigh!
